bull_bear.body:
- Two mature, award-winning assets with long operating track records (Grand Hyatt Goa operational since 2011, Hilton Mumbai since 2001), which the report links to cash flow visibility, revenue predictability and valuation stability
- High-barrier-to-entry locations: North Goa and the Mumbai airport micro-market, where regulatory, environmental and zoning constraints limit incremental quality supply, supporting long-term pricing power
- Affiliation with globally recognised brands (Hyatt, Hilton) providing brand appeal, distribution and mature operating platforms
- Execution credibility inherited from founding promoter Valor Estate Limited — over two decades of land aggregation, municipal clearances and development execution, which the Company says shortens approval timelines and de-risks development
- Institutional, data-driven asset management: standardised KPIs, benchmarking, operator performance reviews and structured investment committees governing capex and repositioning decisions
- In-house project and design teams covering site feasibility, brand selection, design coordination, construction management and delivery, reducing execution risk on brownfield and redevelopment projects
- A rare, contiguous freehold ~5-acre land parcel at Sahar, described as strategically irreplaceable in an extremely supply-constrained micro-market, enabling a commercial development with minimal cash outflow from Advent

- Predominantly domestic demand-driven revenue base with diversified streams (rooms, F&B, MICE), which management cites as insulation from international travel and geopolitical disruption
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Asset and geographic concentration — the entire operating base is two hotels in two micro-markets — The Directors' Report states the Company, through itself and its subsidiaries, owns and operates just two marquee assets — Grand Hyatt Goa (313 keys) and Hilton Mumbai International Airport (171 keys), aggregating 484 keys. Earnings therefore hinge on two properties in Goa and the Mumbai airport precinct, with no revenue diversification across many cities or segments; the Corporate Overview itself cites reducing concentration risk as a reason for pursuing partnerships and new markets.
- Geopolitical disruption to air travel — Management flags that the escalation of the West Asia conflict from February 2026 caused airspace disruptions and flight cancellations, prompting ICRA to revise the aviation industry outlook to Negative in March 2026, and that India-Pakistan tensions briefly elevated geopolitical risk perceptions — which it says it monitors on an ongoing basis. Since both hotels depend on air-linked demand (one is airport-adjacent, one is a fly-in leisure resort), aviation disruption feeds straight into occupancy.
- Deceleration in domestic air passenger growth / aviation capacity constraints — Domestic air passenger traffic in FY2026 grew a modest 1.4% year-on-year to 1,677.4 lakh passengers — a deceleration from prior years — which the report attributes to capacity constraints and geopolitical disruption. Air connectivity is the primary enabler of the leisure and transit demand both properties rely on.
- Exposure of international inbound demand to macro and energy-price shocks — Management names macroeconomic sensitivities — including inflationary pressures from higher energy prices — and the risk of a global economic slowdown as factors that could temper international inbound travel demand. The report cites crude averaging US$82.22/barrel in 2026 versus US$67.74 in 2025 (IMF assumption), a 21% increase, as the source of renewed global inflationary pressure.
- Cyclicality of discretionary travel demand — The report explicitly ties FY26 consumer spending on discretionary categories including travel, leisure and quality dining to a benign inflation environment (FY26 CPI averaging ~2%) and an easing rate cycle (repo cut by a cumulative 100 bps to 5.25%). That framing makes the demand base dependent on a macro configuration that can reverse, and the Directors' Report already notes FY2025-26 saw softer demand across select destinations and temporary disruptions to travel.
- Leverage and refinancing dependence at the subsidiary level — Subsidiaries Goan Hotels & Realty Private Limited and BD & P Hotels (India) Private Limited have only a non-binding, indicative term sheet for a proposed issue of senior secured redeemable non-convertible debentures of up to Rs.740 crore to refinance and consolidate existing borrowings and encumbrances; the Report states the transaction remains subject to due diligence, definitive documents and approvals — so the refinancing is not secured. Operating cash also sits in subsidiaries while the holding company carries finance costs and corporate overheads, and the Board recommended no dividend for the year.
- Rate-led sector cycle with thin occupancy headroom at the Mumbai asset — The sector backdrop described is rate-led rather than occupancy-led — global RevPAR forecast up only 1-2% in 2026 with occupancy broadly flat, and pan-India premium occupancy merely holding at 72-74%. A property already operating near its occupancy ceiling can grow only through ARR, leaving performance hostage to pricing conditions the company does not control.
- Dependence on third-party brand operators and joint-venture partners — The business model is owner-led asset management with operations under globally recognised hospitality brands, which the Company manages through operator oversight mechanisms, standardised KPIs, benchmarking and operator performance reviews to keep operators aligned with owner objectives. Revenue therefore depends on partners' performance and on continuation of those brand affiliations; the commercial development leg similarly depends on a 50:50 joint-venture partner.
- Development and approval execution risk on the pipeline — Three of the five portfolio assets are projects at various stages of planning and development, and the Company describes its in-house capability as reducing execution risk on complex brownfield, urban infill and redevelopment projects that require municipal clearances and stakeholder coordination — an acknowledgement that timelines, costs and approvals are live uncertainties. It also attributes much of its de-risking capability to erstwhile promoter Valor Estate Limited, a relationship that has changed with the demerger.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Advent owns, develops and asset-manages luxury and upper-upscale hospitality assets in India's supply-constrained business and leisure micro-markets, operating them under globally recognised brand partnerships with Hyatt and Hilton rather than managing them itself. Its stated model rests on three pillars: identifying high-potential hospitality and commercial real estate opportunities, developing institutional-quality assets with global brands and established developers, and actively asset-managing them for performance and long-term capital appreciation. Alongside the two operational hotels it is adding a commercial real estate annuity leg via a 50:50 Sahar, Mumbai joint venture, and a hotel development pipeline in Delhi NCR and Mumbai.

outlook.body:
- Evolve from a pure hotel owner into an integrated hospitality and commercial real estate platform — pairing luxury hotel RevPAR growth with the stability and NAV accretion of premium Grade A annuity income

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Advent's portfolio comprises five assets — two operational hotels (Grand Hyatt Goa, 313 keys; Hilton Mumbai International Airport, 171 keys; 484 keys in total) and three projects at various stages of planning and development, including one landmark commercial development. The centrepiece of the pipeline is the Sahar Commercial Development in Mumbai: a 21,978.22 sq mts (~5-acre) freehold land parcel near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, transferred to Advent through the demerger and vested in wholly owned subsidiary Advent Convention and Hotels International Limited, to be developed into a premium Grade A commercial complex of approximately 1.50 million sq ft of leasable area in a 50:50 joint venture with Prestige Estate Projects Limited. The structure is described as minimal cash-outflow for Advent — its major contribution is the land itself while Prestige Estate is to invest Rs.504 crores in cash for its 50% stake, funding the development — and the resulting annuity income is presented as the primary driver of future consolidated EBITDA-margin accretion; no commissioning or completion date is given in this bundle. Separately, the Company says it continued to progress a development pipeline of hotel projects in the Delhi NCR region (in partnership with the Prestige Group) and in Mumbai, and targets scaling to over 2,000 keys under ownership or operational control over the next five years. On the existing estate, FY26 capital expenditure was maintenance and upgrade work at both hotels — strengthening fire and life safety infrastructure, modernising boiler systems with energy-efficient heat pump technology, selective renovation of guest rooms and public areas, and the relaunch of the renovated 'Brasserie' restaurant at Hilton Mumbai (completed during the year); for the coming year management has planned renovation and expansion of accommodation, F&B and event infrastructure at Grand Hyatt Goa. Group structure actions accompanying the expansion plan include acquiring Advent Convention and Hotels International Limited to consolidate the hospitality business under one entity, transferring the entire stake in Marine Tower Properties LLP, and a proposed divestment of the 49% Bamboo Hotel and Global Centre (Delhi) Private Limited holding to reduce related-party payables and the balance-sheet overhang.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects the structural growth drivers of Indian hospitality to persist: rising domestic consumption, expanding air and road connectivity, growing MICE and destination wedding activity, and India's rising prominence as a global tourism destination, while premium supply remains constrained
- Favourable demand-supply balance: Horwath HTL projects chain-affiliated room demand to grow at a 10.6% CAGR through FY29 over FY24 versus supply growth of 8.3%, which the report says underpins sustained pricing power for established luxury operators
- New branded supply is directed away from Advent's markets — of ~8,990 keys opened in CY2025, 64% were in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, leaving luxury and upper-upscale metro supply constrained in Goa, Mumbai and Delhi
- Widening global bifurcation by chain scale favours the premium tier — luxury RevPAR grew ~5.3% through 2025 while the economy segment declined 1.8% — which the report frames as reinforcing the thesis for the segment Advent operates in
- Stabilised-asset premium: hotels operational before FY2021 delivered a 9.2% RevPAR premium over the national average with 71.9% occupancy versus 68%, which the report reads as validating the moat of mature assets like Grand Hyatt Goa and Hilton Mumbai
- MICE supercycle: stabilisation of Jio World Convention Centre, Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi creates a structural step-up in MICE demand expected to sustain elevated occupancies and rate growth over the medium term, which Grand Hyatt Goa and Hilton Mumbai's Chancellor Ballroom are positioned to capture
- Goa has structurally shifted from a seasonal October-March market to a near year-round one as wedding and social MICE demand fills the April-September shoulder months at rates competitive with peak winter
- Goa air connectivity expansion — Mopa's operationalisation and estimated 15-18% YoY growth in combined Goa airport passenger capacity in FY26 — creates additional transient demand for established luxury properties
- Mumbai airport micro-market demand is structural and year-round, with CSIA handling approximately 55+ million passengers annually; commissioning of Navi Mumbai International Airport is expected to broaden the airport-hotel demand base over the medium term
- Rate-led cycle benefits near-ceiling-occupancy assets: CoStar/STR's Q2 2026 forecast of +3.5% RevPAR growth for Mumbai in CY2026 is described as particularly advantageous for airport-proximate hotels that are pure beneficiaries of ARR improvement
- Third-party sector outlook for FY27 (ICRA, March 2026): pan-India premium occupancy holding at 72-74%, ARRs rising to Rs.8,600-8,800, RevPAR to Rs.6,200-6,500 and industry operating margins stable at 34-36%
- Management flags offsetting headwinds: West Asia conflict airspace disruptions, ICRA's Negative aviation outlook from March 2026, decelerating domestic air passenger growth, India-Pakistan tensions, energy-price inflation and global slowdown risk tempering international inbound demand — mitigated, it says, by a predominantly domestic demand base, diversified rooms/F&B/MICE streams and luxury positioning
- Near-term market softness acknowledged: Mumbai ARR down 5-7% YoY as of early 2026 with a modest occupancy pullback, while Goa is in early-stage recovery and has not yet regained its prior peak
- Balance sheet restructuring via the Bamboo Hotel transfer is expected to improve the Debt/EBITDA profile and annual free cash flow, creating financial headroom for disciplined expansion
- Portfolio of five assets: two fully operational hotels and three projects at various stages of planning and development, including one landmark commercial development
- Sahar, Mumbai commercial development — approximately 1.50 million sq ft of Grade A leasable area on a ~5-acre (21,978.22 sq mts) freehold parcel, in a 50:50 JV with Prestige Estate Projects Limited, held through wholly owned subsidiary Advent Convention and Hotels International Limited
- Hotel development pipeline in the Delhi NCR region, in partnership with the Prestige Group, and in Mumbai
- The report states that in respect of the hotel projects described as being in the pipeline, no binding commitment exists as at the date of the report

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Advent Hotels International is a premium, asset-heavy hospitality owner-developer, demerged from Valor Estate Limited and listed in November 2025, that owns two mature branded hotels aggregating 484 keys and is building a Grade A commercial annuity pipeline.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Advent owns, develops and asset-manages luxury and upper-upscale hospitality assets in India's supply-constrained business and leisure micro-markets, operating them under globally recognised brand partnerships with Hyatt and Hilton rather than managing them itself. Its stated model rests on three pillars: identifying high-potential hospitality and commercial real estate opportunities, developing institutional-quality assets with global brands and established developers, and actively asset-managing them for performance and long-term capital appreciation. Alongside the two operational hotels it is adding a commercial real estate annuity leg via a 50:50 Sahar, Mumbai joint venture, and a hotel development pipeline in Delhi NCR and Mumbai.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects the structural growth drivers of Indian hospitality to persist: rising domestic consumption, expanding air and road connectivity, growing MICE and destination wedding activity, and India's rising prominence as a global tourism destination, while premium supply remains constrained
- Favourable demand-supply balance: Horwath HTL projects chain-affiliated room demand to grow at a 10.6% CAGR through FY29 over FY24 versus supply growth of 8.3%, which the report says underpins sustained pricing power for established luxury operators
- New branded supply is directed away from Advent's markets — of ~8,990 keys opened in CY2025, 64% were in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, leaving luxury and upper-upscale metro supply constrained in Goa, Mumbai and Delhi
- Widening global bifurcation by chain scale favours the premium tier — luxury RevPAR grew ~5.3% through 2025 while the economy segment declined 1.8% — which the report frames as reinforcing the thesis for the segment Advent operates in
- Stabilised-asset premium: hotels operational before FY2021 delivered a 9.2% RevPAR premium over the national average with 71.9% occupancy versus 68%, which the report reads as validating the moat of mature assets like Grand Hyatt Goa and Hilton Mumbai
- MICE supercycle: stabilisation of Jio World Convention Centre, Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi creates a structural step-up in MICE demand expected to sustain elevated occupancies and rate growth over the medium term, which Grand Hyatt Goa and Hilton Mumbai's Chancellor Ballroom are positioned to capture
- Goa has structurally shifted from a seasonal October-March market to a near year-round one as wedding and social MICE demand fills the April-September shoulder months at rates competitive with peak winter
- Goa air connectivity expansion — Mopa's operationalisation and estimated 15-18% YoY growth in combined Goa airport passenger capacity in FY26 — creates additional transient demand for established luxury properties
- Mumbai airport micro-market demand is structural and year-round, with CSIA handling approximately 55+ million passengers annually; commissioning of Navi Mumbai International Airport is expected to broaden the airport-hotel demand base over the medium term
- Rate-led cycle benefits near-ceiling-occupancy assets: CoStar/STR's Q2 2026 forecast of +3.5% RevPAR growth for Mumbai in CY2026 is described as particularly advantageous for airport-proximate hotels that are pure beneficiaries of ARR improvement
- Third-party sector outlook for FY27 (ICRA, March 2026): pan-India premium occupancy holding at 72-74%, ARRs rising to Rs.8,600-8,800, RevPAR to Rs.6,200-6,500 and industry operating margins stable at 34-36%
- Management flags offsetting headwinds: West Asia conflict airspace disruptions, ICRA's Negative aviation outlook from March 2026, decelerating domestic air passenger growth, India-Pakistan tensions, energy-price inflation and global slowdown risk tempering international inbound demand — mitigated, it says, by a predominantly domestic demand base, diversified rooms/F&B/MICE streams and luxury positioning
- Near-term market softness acknowledged: Mumbai ARR down 5-7% YoY as of early 2026 with a modest occupancy pullback, while Goa is in early-stage recovery and has not yet regained its prior peak
- Balance sheet restructuring via the Bamboo Hotel transfer is expected to improve the Debt/EBITDA profile and annual free cash flow, creating financial headroom for disciplined expansion
- Portfolio of five assets: two fully operational hotels and three projects at various stages of planning and development, including one landmark commercial development
- Sahar, Mumbai commercial development — approximately 1.50 million sq ft of Grade A leasable area on a ~5-acre (21,978.22 sq mts) freehold parcel, in a 50:50 JV with Prestige Estate Projects Limited, held through wholly owned subsidiary Advent Convention and Hotels International Limited
- Hotel development pipeline in the Delhi NCR region, in partnership with the Prestige Group, and in Mumbai
- The report states that in respect of the hotel projects described as being in the pipeline, no binding commitment exists as at the date of the report

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Evolve from a pure hotel owner into an integrated hospitality and commercial real estate platform — pairing luxury hotel RevPAR growth with the stability and NAV accretion of premium Grade A annuity income
- Scale towards a 2,000+ key portfolio under ownership or operational control, focused on metro cities, airport precincts and premium leisure corridors
- Pursue a capital-efficient growth model: disciplined hotel pipeline additions plus the minimal cash-outflow Sahar commercial development, rather than a single capital-intensive mega-project
- Drive RevPAR and EBITDA improvement at the two existing hotels through the ongoing India hospitality upcycle
- Advance the Sahar commercial development towards timely completion in the 50:50 joint venture with Prestige Estate Projects Limited, contributing land rather than cash
- Simplify the group structure and reduce related-party complexity — consolidating the hospitality business under a single corporate entity and divesting the Bamboo Hotel stake to cut the payable to Valor Estate Limited
- Reinvest continuously in asset quality as long-term owners: fire and life safety infrastructure, energy-efficient boiler/heat-pump modernisation, and selective renovation of guest rooms and public areas
- In FY26 at Grand Hyatt Goa, management deliberately prioritised occupancy and higher-margin F&B and banqueting attachment over headline rate
- Grow through partnerships and management agreements alongside owned assets, to extend footprint with limited capital outlay
- Maintain listed-company governance standards in the first year under SEBI LODR — all mandatory board committees constituted, timely disclosures, and internal control and risk management frameworks

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Advent's portfolio comprises five assets — two operational hotels (Grand Hyatt Goa, 313 keys; Hilton Mumbai International Airport, 171 keys; 484 keys in total) and three projects at various stages of planning and development, including one landmark commercial development. The centrepiece of the pipeline is the Sahar Commercial Development in Mumbai: a 21,978.22 sq mts (~5-acre) freehold land parcel near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, transferred to Advent through the demerger and vested in wholly owned subsidiary Advent Convention and Hotels International Limited, to be developed into a premium Grade A commercial complex of approximately 1.50 million sq ft of leasable area in a 50:50 joint venture with Prestige Estate Projects Limited. The structure is described as minimal cash-outflow for Advent — its major contribution is the land itself while Prestige Estate is to invest Rs.504 crores in cash for its 50% stake, funding the development — and the resulting annuity income is presented as the primary driver of future consolidated EBITDA-margin accretion; no commissioning or completion date is given in this bundle. Separately, the Company says it continued to progress a development pipeline of hotel projects in the Delhi NCR region (in partnership with the Prestige Group) and in Mumbai, and targets scaling to over 2,000 keys under ownership or operational control over the next five years. On the existing estate, FY26 capital expenditure was maintenance and upgrade work at both hotels — strengthening fire and life safety infrastructure, modernising boiler systems with energy-efficient heat pump technology, selective renovation of guest rooms and public areas, and the relaunch of the renovated 'Brasserie' restaurant at Hilton Mumbai (completed during the year); for the coming year management has planned renovation and expansion of accommodation, F&B and event infrastructure at Grand Hyatt Goa. Group structure actions accompanying the expansion plan include acquiring Advent Convention and Hotels International Limited to consolidate the hospitality business under one entity, transferring the entire stake in Marine Tower Properties LLP, and a proposed divestment of the 49% Bamboo Hotel and Global Centre (Delhi) Private Limited holding to reduce related-party payables and the balance-sheet overhang.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Two mature, award-winning assets with long operating track records (Grand Hyatt Goa operational since 2011, Hilton Mumbai since 2001), which the report links to cash flow visibility, revenue predictability and valuation stability
- High-barrier-to-entry locations: North Goa and the Mumbai airport micro-market, where regulatory, environmental and zoning constraints limit incremental quality supply, supporting long-term pricing power
- Affiliation with globally recognised brands (Hyatt, Hilton) providing brand appeal, distribution and mature operating platforms
- Execution credibility inherited from founding promoter Valor Estate Limited — over two decades of land aggregation, municipal clearances and development execution, which the Company says shortens approval timelines and de-risks development
- Institutional, data-driven asset management: standardised KPIs, benchmarking, operator performance reviews and structured investment committees governing capex and repositioning decisions
- In-house project and design teams covering site feasibility, brand selection, design coordination, construction management and delivery, reducing execution risk on brownfield and redevelopment projects
- A rare, contiguous freehold ~5-acre land parcel at Sahar, described as strategically irreplaceable in an extremely supply-constrained micro-market, enabling a commercial development with minimal cash outflow from Advent
- Balanced model of owned assets plus partnerships and management agreements, allowing footprint growth with limited capital outlay
- Predominantly domestic demand-driven revenue base with diversified streams (rooms, F&B, MICE), which management cites as insulation from international travel and geopolitical disruption

A property already operating near its occupancy ceiling can grow only through ARR, leaving performance hostage to pricing conditions the company does not control.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
